candidate.answerReason: The two rectangles each have perimeter 12 inches and share a 2-inch edge. Removing both copies of that internal edge gives 12 + 12 - 4 = 20 inches.

methods.label: Remove the shared edge
methods.explanation:
Only the outside boundary contributes to the perimeter of the T. Each \(2\times4\) rectangle has perimeter
\[
2(2+4)=12\text{ inches}.
\]
The rectangles meet along the stem's \(2\)-inch top edge. Adding their perimeters counts this shared edge twice, but it lies inside the T and should not be counted. Removing both copies gives
\[
12+12-2\cdot2=\boxed{20}\text{ inches}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses rectangle perimeters and elementary reasoning about which edges belong to the outside boundary.

candidate.annotationRationale: The central target is finding the perimeter of joined rectangles while excluding their shared edge. The catalog supplies individual rectangle perimeters through cnm_p078 and rectangle side properties through cnm_p077. These support the written method, but neither explicitly captures the composite-perimeter target, so a missing node is proposed.

needsNewNodes.name: Perimeter of joined rectangles
needsNewNodes.description: Find the perimeter of a figure formed by joining nonoverlapping rectangles along edges. Count each exposed boundary segment once and exclude shared segments; equivalently, subtract twice the shared length from the sum of the individual perimeters.
needsNewNodes.reason: The catalog covers individual rectangle and square perimeters but lacks the shared-boundary reasoning needed for the perimeter of the T.
